questions.q: State the formula for eccentricity of an ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) with \(a > b\), and give the coordinates of its foci.
questions.a: Eccentricity \(e = \frac{\sqrt{a^2 - b^2}}{a}\), foci are \((\pm \sqrt{a^2 - b^2}, 0)\). A wrong answer like \(e = \frac{\sqrt{b^2 - a^2}}{a}\) or foci at \((0, \pm c)\) reveals confusion about which axis is major and the condition \(a > b\).

questions.q: Explain why the eccentricity of an ellipse is always less than 1, using the relationship \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\).
questions.a: Since \(a > b > 0\), \(c = \sqrt{a^2 - b^2} < a\), so \(e = c/a < 1\). If a student says \(e > 1\) or uses \(c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}\), they are confusing ellipse with hyperbola or misapplying the Pythagorean relation.

questions.q: Find the eccentricity, foci, and directrices of the ellipse \(4x^2 + 9y^2 = 36\).
questions.a: Divide by 36: \(\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1\). Here \(a^2 = 9, b^2 = 4 \Rightarrow a=3, b=2\). \(c = \sqrt{9-4} = \sqrt{5}\). \(e = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\). Foci: \((\pm \sqrt{5}, 0)\). Directrices: \(x = \pm \frac{3}{\sqrt{5}/3} = \pm \frac{9}{\sqrt{5}}\). A wrong answer with \(a=2, b=3\) shows inability to identify the larger denominator as \(a^2\).

questions.q: An ellipse has foci at \((\pm 4, 0)\) and eccentricity \(e = \frac{2}{3}\). Find its equation and directrices.
questions.a: Given \(c = 4\), \(e = c/a = 2/3 \Rightarrow a = 6\). Then \(b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 36 - 16 = 20\). Equation: \(\frac{x^2}{36} + \frac{y^2}{20} = 1\). Directrices: \(x = \pm a/e = \pm 6/(2/3) = \pm 9\). If a student uses \(b\) instead of \(a\) in \(e = c/a\), they will get incorrect \(a\) and \(b\).

questions.q: A student claims that for the ellipse \(\frac{x^2}{16} + \frac{y^2}{25} = 1\), the foci are \((\pm 3, 0)\) and directrices are \(x = \pm \frac{16}{3}\). Evaluate this claim.
questions.a: The claim is false. Here \(b^2 = 25 > a^2 = 16\), so major axis is y-axis. \(c = \sqrt{25-16} = 3\). Foci: \((0, \pm 3)\). \(e = c/b = 3/5\). Directrices: \(y = \pm b/e = \pm 25/3\). The student incorrectly assumed major axis along x-axis.

questions.q: Construct a real-world problem where an elliptical arch of a bridge has a span of 20 m and height 8 m at the center. Ask for the distance from the center to the foci and the equations of the directrices.
questions.a: Span = 20 m \(\Rightarrow\) semi-major axis \(a = 10\) m (horizontal). Height = 8 m \(\Rightarrow\) semi-minor axis \(b = 8\) m. \(c = \sqrt{100-64} = 6\) m. Foci at \((\pm 6, 0)\). \(e = 6/10 = 0.6\). Directrices: \(x = \pm a/e = \pm 10/0.6 = \pm 50/3\) m. A poor answer would use \(a=8, b=10\) or forget to halve the span.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The receiver must be placed at a ______ to collect signals.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can compute eccentricity, coordinates of foci, and equations of directrices for any ellipse given in standard or general form, and can use these to solve real-world problems involving elliptical orbits, arches, or reflective properties.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: The ______ must be placed at a focus to collect signals.
